description: The same recipient typed entirely in capitals, with no display name and no angle brackets, collapses to the plain-lowercase first-send delivery key.
why_it_exists: wf4-delivery-key-recipient-normalisation pins the display-name/angle-bracket variant, which exercises the angle-bracket extraction in normEmail() and only incidentally its toLowerCase(). The bare ALL CAPS form is the one a practitioner produces by copying an address out of a scanned insurer letterhead or a caps-locked field, and until now nothing pinned it. If the lowercasing were ever dropped while the angle-bracket extraction stayed, that existing scenario would still pass and this delivery would look new - the same letter sent to the same insurer twice, with no duplicate detectable in the register.

input.sanitisation_note: The address is the same 27-character synthetic address used by wf4-delivery-key-first-send and wf4-delivery-key-recipient-normalisation, written in upper case. No real recipient appears here.

assertions: send_key is identical to the plain-lowercase first-send key
normEmail() lowercases an address that carries no display name and no angle brackets
the channel is uppercased before entering the basis
